newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: High winds impede Venezuelan oil spill rescue.
newsitem.headline: High winds impede Venezuelan oil spill rescue.

text.p: High winds hindered attempts Monday evening to stem the flow of crude oil from a ruptured tanker which ran aground on Friday near the Venezuelan coast, oil company officials said.

The Greek-registered Nissos Amorgos, chartered by Italian oil company Agip a subsidiary of ENI, went aground just before midnight on Friday near the mouth of Lake Maracaibo in northwestern Venezuela, spilling about 25,000 barrels of crude, according to a statement by Venezuela's state oil subsidiary Maraven.
Venezuela's Navy said the volume of the spill increased to at least 60,000 barrels on Saturday when the ship was towed about 100 miles (150 kilometres) eastwards for repairs.

"On its voyage towards Guaranao, the coastguards ordered the tanker to anchor on the high seas, 16 miles from the Paraguana coast, when they realised the ship was still spilling oil," the Maraven statement said.
Maraven said poor weather had hindred attempts to patch the tanker's shell with specially-built metal sheets. Barges and a trans-shipment tanker were also on the scene, it said.
Divers found large holes affecting at least two tanks in the ship, Maraven added, but a spokesman said he did not know if oil was still flowing from the striken tanker on Monday night.

In Zulia state, site of the original spill, Maraven said that up to 9.3 miles (15 kilometres) of coastline were polluted with crude oil. State press agency Venpres said the coastline of neighbouring Falcon state, where the tanker is anchored, had not yet been affected.

The 10-year-old Nissos Amorgos was carrying 476,000 barrels of heavy crude from Venezuela's Bachaquero field to Agip's Gela port in Italy. Maraven said the oil was sold "free on board" meaning that ownership passed to Agip at the loading terminal.
Nissos Amorgos conformed to the requirements of MARPOL, an international maritime oil pollution agreement, and had recently sailed to the United States, Maraven added.
